To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the emotional responses to music are reflected in the chaotic dynamics of the brain.

the emotional response to 1/f music was reflected in the chaotic dynamics of the electrical activity of the brain, and that the chaotic dynamics were more complex for 1/f music than for white music or brown music.

the chaotic dynamics of EEGs during perception of music are related to the emotional responses and that the rhythm variations of music are more important to a pleasing response than the melody variations.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the quantification of the emotional response to 1/f music and its relationship to brain function.
the quantification of emotion and the way in which it is reflected in the brain.
the relationship between music and emotion and with the way in which music affects the electrical activity of the human brain.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the chaotic behavior of brain electrical activities is a reflection of emotional responses to music.
the chaotic dynamics of the EEG are decreased by a pleasant emotional response to music.
the chaotic dynamics of the brain is decreased during the perception of 1/ f music.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
chaos is a good measure for the emotional response to 1/f music.
the chaotic dynamics of EEGs elicited by music are related to the perception of emotion.
1/f rhythms are more pleasing than 1/f melodies.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the nonlinear measures of the EEGs elicited by 1/f music are lower than those of the EEGs by white or brown music and that this difference is statistically significant.
nonlinear methods are useful for quantifying emotion, especially the pleasantness of music, by measuring brain activity.
the brain's chaotic dynamics can be used to quantify emotion and that the chaotic electrophysiology elicited by the music can be used to measure how much the listener likes the music.
